story_type: elderly sailor and dog, disabled sailboat far offshore
hook: A 77-year-old sailor and his dog, 120 miles out at sea
narration: A seventy-seven-year-old sailor and his dog, a hundred and twenty miles out.
A ham radio operator in Texas overheard his mayday call.
A Coast Guard Jayhawk crew found his sailboat drifting in a shipping lane.
The mast was damaged. The sails were torn, and some were trailing in the water.
He could not survive out there, with no supplies and no way to sail.
But the boat was his home, and he did not want to leave.
So they lowered their rescue swimmer into the sea to talk with him.
Hoisting over a sailboat is risky, because a swaying mast can snag the cable.
He climbed into the basket, and the crew hoisted him up through the broken rigging.
outcome: The sailor and his dog were both hoisted aboard and flown safely back to San Diego.
title: Adrift 120 miles out with his dog
description:
On March 21, 2011, a Coast Guard MH-60 Jayhawk crew from Sector San Diego rescued a 77-year-old man and his dog from a disabled sailboat adrift about 120 miles southwest of San Diego. Both were hoisted from the boat and flown safely to San Diego.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 2nd Class Henry G. Dunphy, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/133684/coast-guard-top-videos-2011-sailboat-rescue
